raw: 40.1 The Cognitive Attack Surface: Attention, Memory, Trust, and Decision-Making[^95]
teaching_note: Attack surface is a defensive organizing metaphor here: competing demands may affect attention, repetition may affect familiarity, authority cues may affect trust, and incomplete information may affect decisions. These are hypotheses about processes, not observations of anyone's private mental state. Ordinary error, satire, accessibility problems, and legitimate disagreement remain alternatives; the policy paper does not validate a detector for manipulation or person-level susceptibility [@ageint095].
title: The Cognitive Attack Surface: Attention, Memory, Trust, and Decision-Making

raw: 40.2 Adversarial Cognitive Operations: PSYOP, Active Measures, Synthetic Influence[^105]
teaching_note: Historical and doctrinal terms describe different institutional practices and contexts; they are not interchangeable labels for every false post. Separate a content finding, a distribution pattern, and an actor-attribution claim, each of which needs its own evidence. This lesson examines supplied records for possible information harms without producing messages, testing influence on people, or inferring an operation from unpopular views alone [@ageint105].
title: Adversarial Cognitive Operations: Defensive Recognition and Attribution Limits

raw: 40.3 Deepfakes, Voice Cloning, and Digital Identity Attacks
teaching_note: **Completed synthetic media triage.** At 10:00 packet M contains a fictional aquarium voice clip claiming tomorrow's closure; M2 copies the same clip, a supplied detector flags it 0.82, and no provenance credential is present. The triage record separates media authenticity (unresolved), closure truth (unconfirmed), speaker authorization (unknown), and actor intent (unknown); neither a detector score nor missing credentials proves fabrication. Decision: preserve the supplied originals and metadata, group M/M2 as one origin, and hold both the closure claim and any public accusation. At 10:30 instructor card O, an independent fictional operations schedule, confirms a closure for repairs but does not authenticate the clip, so draft v2 corrects the closure fact while retaining all three other unknowns. No real contact, voice matching, identity search, automatic response, or dissemination occurs; generic software-security citations are governance context, while the domain anchors discuss deepfake risk and limitations [@official_nsa_cisa_contextualizing_deepfake_threats; @scholarly_cardenuto_2023_synthetic_realities].
title: Deepfakes, Voice Cloning, and Digital Identity Attacks

raw: 40.4 From Spycraft to Self-Mastery: SATs for Personal Cognitive Security[^188]
teaching_note: A key-assumptions check can expose that 'a familiar voice is authorized' and 'an authentic recording must be current' are separate, defeasible assumptions. Applying it to the aquarium packet changes the release decision without claiming to cure bias or reveal an author's intent. The popular account supplies a practical analogy, not experimental proof that SATs improve every everyday decision; use the explicit procedure and stop rules in [@sec:analytic-workflow] [@ageint188].
title: SATs for Personal Cognitive Security: Reviewable Reasoning, Not Self-Diagnosis

teaching_note: Organizational resilience is a capacity to notice, question, correct, and recover from information failures, not a workforce belief score. In the aquarium case, a versioned handoff stating which fact changed and which authenticity questions did not is more defensible than declaring the incident solved. Treat accessible reporting and correction channels as proposed controls whose effects need evaluation; do not equate policy adoption or attendance with demonstrated resistance [@ageint095].
title: Building Organizational Cognitive Resilience

raw: 40.6 National Cognitive Security Centers: Policy Proposals[^95]
teaching_note: A proposed center is an institutional design, not evidence that such centers exist everywhere, are necessary, or are effective. Compare its suggested remit with narrower arrangements such as independent correction services, asking who sets standards, hears appeals, and prevents mission creep. Any authority to collect, intervene, or restrict information would require separate jurisdiction-specific legal analysis; this policy citation supplies no operational authorization [@ageint095].
title: National Cognitive Security Centers: Policy Proposals

raw: 40.7 Cognitive Security and Active Inference: The Predictive Mind Under Attack[^106][^3]
teaching_note: Active inference supplies a vocabulary of generative models, beliefs, observations, and policies for studying perception and action. A human analogy, a thesis review, and an implemented agent model are different evidence classes; a coherent explanation does not establish that a particular person's beliefs were manipulated or that an AI intervention is safe. Keep model assumptions explicit and do not derive persuasion tactics, clinical claims, or human-agent equivalence from the vocabulary [@ageint106; @ageint003].
title: Cognitive Security and Active Inference: Modeling Perspective

raw: 40.8 AI-Assisted Cognitive Security Tools: Detection and Intervention Systems[^96]
teaching_note: AI may help extract dates, group duplicates, or propose alternative readings of the supplied aquarium records; its generated explanation is not an independent source. Evaluate a detector with known labels, error denominators, false alarms, and task/population limits before treating scores as evidence, and abstain when those inputs are missing. The cited position paper proposes a research agenda rather than validated detection or intervention performance; no automatic accusation, targeted messaging, or live response follows [@ageint096].
title: AI-Assisted Cognitive Security: Assistance, Detection Limits, and Human Review
